headline: Evidence is the basis for knowledge—what we see, measure, and verify about reality
universal_truth: Claims without evidence are opinions; the strength of your belief should match the strength of your evidence
fun_facts: Scientists require evidence to be reproducible—others must be able to get the same results
Anecdotes are the weakest form of evidence—one case doesn't prove a pattern
Confirmation bias leads us to notice evidence for what we already believe and ignore evidence against
discussion_questions: How do you evaluate evidence for claims you hear?
What do you believe without good evidence?
How do you distinguish between strong and weak evidence?

hook.script: Anyone can claim anything. What separates knowledge from belief? Evidence. Observations, measurements, experiments—things we can verify, test, and replicate. Evidence is how we know what's actually true.

cliff.script: We're flooded with claims—in news, online, from friends. How do we know what to believe?

options.text: Claims should be proportional to evidence—extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence; the strength of belief should match the quality and quantity of supporting evidence
options.response: Yes. A claim that it will rain tomorrow needs modest evidence. A claim that aliens visited needs extraordinary evidence. Match confidence to evidence quality.
Reliable sources help, but the best approach is understanding their evidence, not just their reputation...

fact1.title: Evidence Hierarchy
fact1.script: Not all evidence is equal. Anecdotes are weak. Case studies are better. Controlled experiments are better still. Replicated, peer-reviewed studies are strongest. Know the hierarchy.

fact2.title: Confirmation Bias
fact2.script: We naturally notice evidence for what we believe and dismiss evidence against. Fighting this bias requires actively seeking disconfirming evidence, not just confirming.

fact3.title: Proportional Belief
fact3.script: Strong evidence warrants strong belief. Weak evidence warrants tentative belief. No evidence warrants no belief. Calibrate your confidence to your evidence.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Claims without evidence are opinions. The strength of your belief should match the strength of your evidence. Demand evidence.

outro.script: That's Day 294. Tomorrow, we'll explore guesses you can test—hypotheses. Until then, examine the evidence for something you believe.

growTrack.title: Evidence Audit - What Do You Really Know?
growTrack.learning_objective: Evaluate the evidence basis for current beliefs
growTrack.activity: Pick a belief you hold strongly. What's the evidence for it? What's the evidence against it? Have you sought disconfirming evidence? Is your confidence calibrated to your evidence?
